sources.excerpt: The Great Wall of China: Visible from Space? A long-standing claim, often repeated in popular

reasoning: The claim that the Great Wall of China is the only man-made structure visible from space with the naked eye is a well-documented myth. NASA, astronaut testimonies (including China's first astronaut, Yang Liwei), and optical physics confirm that the Great Wall is not visible from low Earth orbit with the unaided eye. At only about 5 to 9 meters wide and constructed from local stone and earth, the wall blends in with the surrounding terrain and lacks sufficient visual contrast. In contrast, larger or higher-contrast man-made structures—such as major highways, large airport runways, large dams, greenhouse complexes, and city lights at night—can be seen from orbit under favorable conditions.
